Cathie Wood bought Kalshi before she started using it 💸📊
The news 🗞️ The recent ARK’s Kalshi deal got mostly reported as prediction markets going institutional. But the sequence is the whole story here.
Let’s unpack this.
More on this 👉 In December 2025, ARK joined Kalshi’s $1 billion Series E at an $11 billion valuation, alongside Paradigm, Sequoia, and a16z. In March 2026, ARK became the flagship institutional customer, using a new “market request pipeline” to commission custom contracts on non-farm payrolls, deficit-to-GDP, and company KPIs in genomics and AI. Four months between buying the equity and validating the product publicly.
Press coverage separates the two events. It shouldn’t.
We must remember that five weeks before ARK’s announcement, Fed economists published a paper finding Kalshi outperformed Bloomberg consensus on CPI and held a perfect pre-FOMC forecast record against Fed Funds futures.
That’s the legitimizing event. Kalshi went from $2 billion in July to $5 billion in October to $11 billion in December, repriced not as a betting venue but as financial data infrastructure. Nick Grous calling the prices “purest expressions of risk” reads differently when ARK owns the cap table.
Zoom out 🔎 The ecosystem loop is perhaps the most interesting part. ARK’s public usage validates Kalshi to other institutions, deepens liquidity, expands TAM beyond retail into the full research stack, and marks up ARK’s own stake.
It’s classic venture-portfolio play run through a publicly disclosed asset manager. Nothing improper about it, but the “research partnership” framing obscures that ARK has two reasons to want this to work 😎
THE TAKEAWAY ✈️
What’s next? 🤔 Looking ahead, most people focus on whether sell-side research or Bloomberg gets displaced. The more important question though is compliance. Banks have started applying insider trading rules to prediction market positions, and the CFTC issued an enforcement advisory in February citing nonpublic information misuse on Kalshi. Every PM who wants to trade a company-KPI contract now has an MNPI question their compliance desk hasn’t answered. That’s the real friction, not pipeline infrastructure. Zooming out, watch ICE’s $2 billion Polymarket stake too; NYSE’s parent sees this as infrastructure worth owning, not a data feed worth renting. Kalshi’s moat has to become institutional integration, because regulatory legitimacy is about to commoditize.
ICYMI: 
Robinhood’s OpenAI bet is really a bet on itself 🤖💰
Following the money 💸 The walls between retail investors and private markets didn’t come down last week. The SEC knocked them down months ago. Robinhood just walked through first.
Let’s take a look at this.
More on this 👉 Robinhood Ventures Fund I just closed a $75 million purchase of OpenAI common stock - actual equity, not the synthetic tokens that drew OpenAI’s public rebuke last summer. RVI shares jumped as much as 20% on the news. The fund, which listed in March at $25 per share and promptly sank to $22, suddenly had a reason to exist in the eyes of the market.
The backstory matters here.
In June 2025, Robinhood launched tokenized OpenAI shares for European users. OpenAI’s response on X was blunt: these aren’t our shares, we didn’t approve this, be careful. Ten months later, Robinhood holds real OpenAI common stock inside a registered fund with full regulatory blessing. That’s a remarkable rehabilitation of a relationship that started with a cease-and-desist tone.
Zoom out 🔎 But the OpenAI position is just the shiny object here. The deeper story is structural. Last year, the SEC dropped its 15% cap on closed-end funds’ private market allocations and eliminated accredited investor requirements for these vehicles. Robinhood had a $658 million fund ready to deploy the moment the door opened. The fund charges a 2% management fee on net assets, no performance fee. For a company whose revenue has historically swung with trading volumes, that’s a quieter, stickier revenue stream - and one that scales with every marquee name added to the portfolio.
OpenAI, valued at $852 billion after its $122 billion March round, is expected to file for an IPO targeting $1 trillion as early as late 2026. RVI’s stated plan is to hold through IPO and beyond. If that works, the fund becomes the proof of concept for a product category every brokerage will need to match.
THE TAKEAWAY ✈️
What’s next? 🤔 Looking ahead, here’s what to watch. NAV premium/discount dynamics will tell you whether the market treats RVI as a real investment vehicle or a meme trade on private market FOMO. If RVI trades persistently above NAV, Robinhood launches Fund II. If it doesn’t, the democratization thesis gets a lot harder to sell. Meanwhile, Fidelity and Schwab are watching closely. The $80 trillion retail asset pool that the World Economic Forum keeps citing is about to get a lot more pitches. That said, the key question now isn’t whether private markets are open to retail. It’s whether retail investors understand what they’re buying when the asset can’t be priced in real time and can’t be sold in a crisis. That’s the key here.
ICYMI: Robinhood: the $4.5 billion revenue dark horse that Wall Street still underestimates [ https://substack.com/redirect/37972fb0-8d4c-46c6-9e8a-9b3120e66fcb?j=eyJ1IjoiOGFiMHN3In0.zP6ncAt57e5BSjUJ_SVakLp2EJCK6mdxH_GkAgT_Z5c ] 🤷‍♂️📉 [ https://substack.com/redirect/37972fb0-8d4c-46c6-9e8a-9b3120e66fcb?j=eyJ1IjoiOGFiMHN3In0.zP6ncAt57e5BSjUJ_SVakLp2EJCK6mdxH_GkAgT_Z5c ] [deep dive into their Q4 & full year 2025 financials, what stands out, and why I’m still really bullish]
🧠 What else I’m watching
Piraeus Launches AI Innovation Hub 🤖 Piraeus Bank has inaugurated an AI hub with Accenture and Anthropic [ https://substack.com/redirect/f7f2c1c9-b130-49e4-95cd-eaa4befcf935?j=eyJ1IjoiOGFiMHN3In0.zP6ncAt57e5BSjUJ_SVakLp2EJCK6mdxH_GkAgT_Z5c ] to transition from isolated AI projects to an enterprise-wide capability. The hub will drive AI innovation across operations, customer experience, risk, and compliance, while modernizing the bank’s technology stack. Leveraging Udacity, Accenture’s AI training platform, Piraeus aims to embed AI skills organization-wide. ICYMI: 
Moonfare Launches AI Investment Strategy 🚀 Moonfare has unveiled an AI-focused early and growth stage strategy, offering diversified exposure to artificial intelligence and transformative innovation. The portfolio combines 8–15 top-tier venture and growth managers - selected for their track records in scaling category-defining tech - and 8–15 co-investments sourced through Moonfare’s GP network. The strategy targets key themes like AI, cybersecurity, next-gen healthcare, deep tech, fintech infrastructure, and physical AI. ICYMI: 
Aurionpro Revolutionizes Trade Finance 🤖 Aurionpro has launched Fintra, an AI-native trade finance platform that automates document processing, compliance, clause recommendations, and risk scoring using specialized AI agents, while ensuring human governance at every decision. Built on Aurion AI -an AI-native banking software stack - the platform integrates with core systems like SWIFT and General Ledger. Fintra introduces the Confidence-Gated Handoff Protocol (CGHP), which evaluates each decision’s confidence, materiality, and regulatory compliance before routing to human oversight, with full auditability. The platform is now available for pilot engagements with banks in India, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia, with additional AI-native solutions planned for corporate lending, retail lending, and supply chain finance. ICYMI:

subject: I Built a Stock Risk Auditor with Claude
full_body:
View this post on the web at https://news.aiinvestinghq.com/p/i-built-a-stock-risk-auditor-with

Most people go from “I get the business” to “I like the stock” way too fast.
I don’t.
This is what my investing research process with AI usually looks like:
1. Understand the business:
AI helps me build an of how the company makes money and what drives economics.
2. Decide if it deserves deeper work:
After the overview, I decide if this stock is worth going deeper or not.
3. Read the annual report properly:
AI helps me go beyond the story and into the real disclosures, footnotes, and accounting.
4. Map the risks before conviction:
While I read the report, AI helps me build the downside map in parallel:
what already looks fragile
which disclosures deserve a closer read
what questions I still need answered before conviction forms
5. Build the bull thesis :AI helps me turn the research into a clear upside case.
6. Stress-test it hard :AI helps me challenge my own thesis before I trust it.
This article is about step 4.
I built a Claude Skill called Stock Risk Auditor.
You run it with one command.
Claude then spends ~10 minutes doing the hard work in the background.
And let’s be honest: that’s a much better use of AI than asking it for “the next 10x stock.”
The output is a full Stock Risk Audit. Not a recycled “risk factors” section.
It gives you:
the top risks ranked by importance across the business, the balance sheet, and the external environment
a final risk label (Low / Moderate / Elevated)
In this article, I’ll show you how it works first.
Then you can take the skill, drop it into Claude, and use it in your next stock analysis knowing exactly what it’s doing.
Let’s dive in:
How the Stock Risk Audit Works:
If you’ve never used a Claude Skill before, don’t worry.
A Claude Skill is basically a saved workflow inside Claude.
Instead of rewriting the same prompts every time, you install it once and run it when you need it.
That’s exactly what I’m giving you in this article.
How to use it :
Open Claude
Claude Web is enough.
You do not need Claude Desktop or Claude Code.
 Start a new chat 
Click the “+” button and select the skill
Choose the skill from your saved skills.
(You’ll need to install it first by uploading my file, but I cover that at the end of this article.)
 Give it the stock name or ticker
For example:CrowdStrike
Wait 10 minutes( Go do something else, Claude doesn’t need emotional support)
Result: a 7–8 page Stock Risk Audit, structured the way I designed it inside the skill.
My favorite part of the report is the final section: Next Deep-Dive Questions.
For CrowdStrike for exemple, one question was:
Can CrowdStrike keep charging premium prices if Microsoft makes Defender “good enough” inside Windows?
That’s useful.
Because the report doesn’t just tell you “there is risk.”
It tells you where to investigate next.
But Mostapha, how do I know that this is not just AI slop in a nice wrapper?
Fair question.
I’ve been using AI for investing for more than a year.
And from the outside, it’s hard to tell the difference between:
a random prompt from someone who never seriously analyzed a stock
and a real workflow built by an investor, tested across multiple stocks.
The difference is the structure behind it:
This is not one giant prompt asking Claude to “find risks.”
It’s a small research system inside Claude:
1. One main instruction file :It tells Claude the job, the rules, the ranking logic, and the final memo format.
2. Three tested investing prompts: These are prompts I had already refined and tested for 8+ months in my investing process. 
Business risk: what could weaken the operating engine
Financial risk: what could stress cash flow, dilution, or the balance sheet
Structural / external risk: what outside forces could change the economics
3. One synthesis step
Claude merges the three passes into one ranked Stock Risk Audit.
So the skill is not magic.
It is:
one main instruction file + 3 tested prompts + one final risk memo.
Now that you know how it works, let’s install the skill.

 CME Group TOP 5 INSIGHTS: The Most Important Recent Events

First-quarter average daily volume reached about 36 million contracts, up about 22%, and March hit about 41 million, up about 33%. 2️⃣ 🧲 Recent numbers also show deeper customer use, not just fast trading. Open interest rose to about 126 million contracts, up about 6% year over year, and large holders reached about 3,616. That matters because it means more positions are staying inside CME’s ecosystem, which is a stronger sign than volume alone.

It matters more than a flashy product launch because it can make the company more useful in daily institutional workflow.
4️⃣ 🛠️ The clearest recent negative was the temporary technical halt in metals and natural-gas trading. For a market utility, even a short outage matters because trust is part of the product. Still, trading resumed the same day, so this looks more like a temporary setback than long-term structural damage.
5️⃣ 📈 Taken together, recent events make CME look broader and deeper than a pure volatility beneficiary.
